original_question: Suppose X has a normalized Schauder basis (x_n) such that every normalized block sequence of (x_n) spans a subspace isomorphic to X. Must X itself be isomorphic to c_0 or to l_p for some 1 <= p < infinity?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6 ("Block homogeneous basis problem"), stated immediately after the paper's definition of a block homogeneous Schauder basis.
correct_elements: Your draft already isolates the right open problem and is very close to the paper's wording. It has the correct hypothesis: X has a normalized Schauder basis such that every normalized block sequence of that basis spans a subspace isomorphic to X. It also has the correct conclusion: whether this forces X to be isomorphic to c_0 or to ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞.
missing_details: State explicitly that X is a Banach space, in the usual real-or-complex Banach-space setting of the paper.
Make explicit that the basis (x_n) is normalized, i.e. ||x_n|| = 1 for every n.
Define 'normalized block sequence of (x_n)': each y_k is a finitely supported linear combination of successive basis vectors from (x_n), the supports are strictly increasing, and ||y_k|| = 1.
Clarify that 'spans a subspace isomorphic to X' means the closed linear span [y_k] is isomorphic to X as a Banach space.
Record the paper's exact shorthand for this hypothesis: the basis is called 'block homogeneous'.
Make clear that no extra assumptions such as reflexivity, unconditionality, or equivalence of each block sequence to the original basis are part of this problem.
refined_question: Let X be a real or complex Banach space with a normalized Schauder basis (x_n). Assume that for every normalized block sequence (y_n) of (x_n) — that is, each y_n is a norm-1 finitely supported linear combination of successive basis vectors x_i, with strictly increasing supports — the closed linear span [y_n] is isomorphic to X. Must X be isomorphic to c_0 or to ℓ_p for some 1 ≤ p < ∞?
justification: This is the paper's Section 6 open problem, not a broader neighboring question. The draft matches the block-subspace/isomorphism formulation of Problem 6 almost verbatim. It is stronger than the Rosenthal-basis condition from Section 4, where one only asks that every normalized block sequence have a subsequence equivalent to the basis, and it is also different from Zippin's perfectly homogeneous hypothesis, where every normalized block sequence is itself equivalent to the basis. The only real sharpening needed is to make the standard Banach-space conventions and the definition of 'normalized block sequence' explicit so the question stands alone exactly as intended in the paper.
